## 1. Verdict

- Usable observed PM2.5: **7.44 years** (65,214 hours)
- Threshold for proceeding as planned: **2.0 years**
- **Gate: PASS**

Dhaka has sufficient contiguous coverage to serve as the primary dataset.
Beijing (UCI) is retained for the cross-city generalisation check.

## 3. Contiguity and gaps

| Quantity | Value |
|---|---|
| Number of distinct gaps | 2,074 |
| Longest gap | **2,712 hours** (113.0 days) |
| Longest gap start (UTC) | 2022-05-31 19:00:00+00:00 |
| Longest gap end (UTC) | 2022-09-21 18:00:00+00:00 |
| Longest unbroken observed run | **1,715 hours** (71.5 days) |
| Longest run start (UTC) | 2020-09-04 16:00:00+00:00 |
| Longest run end (UTC) | 2020-11-15 02:00:00+00:00 |

Gaps matter twice over: they bound how long an input window can be, and
any window spanning one is fabricated data. Gap-aware windowing rejects
those windows and reports the count.

### Gap length distribution

| gap_length   |   n_gaps |   hours_lost |
|:-------------|---------:|-------------:|
| 1 h          |     1324 |         1324 |
| 2-3 h        |      456 |         1030 |
| 4-24 h       |      240 |         2330 |
| 1-7 d        |       43 |         2286 |
| > 7 d        |       11 |         7032 |

The gap count alone is misleading. Most outages are single hours; only
11 exceed a week.
Applying the configured backward-looking forward-fill limit of
3 hours raises coverage from 82.3% to
86.4% and collapses 2,074 fragments into
295 usable stretches, lengthening the longest from
1,715 h to 4,283 h.

results should be read with that in mind: the wet-season sample is drawn
from eight monsoons, not nine.

## 4. Quality-control ledger

Every filter, with the rows it removed. Applied in this order.

| rule                      |   removed |   remaining | note                                          |
|:--------------------------|----------:|------------:|:----------------------------------------------|
| raw records               |         0 |       81808 |                                               |
| parameter != pm25         |     11525 |       70283 |                                               |
| value is NaN              |         0 |       70283 |                                               |
| negative value            |      5056 |       65227 |                                               |
| exact zero (sensor fault) |        13 |       65214 |                                               |
| above sanity cap 1000     |         0 |       65214 |                                               |
| flatline run > 12         |         0 |       65214 | (consecutive identical values = stuck sensor) |
| duplicate timestamps      |         0 |       65214 | (overlap between concatenated location IDs)   |

**Note on negative values.** 5,056 readings (7.2% of PM2.5
records) were negative and were dropped. Beta-attenuation monitors
routinely report small negatives near the detection limit, so this is
expected instrument behaviour rather than corruption; it is recorded
here because dropping rather than flooring them is a modelling choice.

### Meteorology (NASA POWER)

| variable          |   observed |   missing |   pct_missing |
|:------------------|-----------:|----------:|--------------:|
| T2M               |  87672.000 |     0.000 |         0.000 |
| T2MDEW            |  87672.000 |     0.000 |         0.000 |
| RH2M              |  87672.000 |     0.000 |         0.000 |
| WS10M             |  87672.000 |     0.000 |         0.000 |
| WD10M             |  87672.000 |     0.000 |         0.000 |
| PS                |  87672.000 |     0.000 |         0.000 |
| PRECTOTCORR       |  87672.000 |     0.000 |         0.000 |
| ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN |  87672.000 |     0.000 |         0.000 |

Units as reported by the POWER API (quoted verbatim, not assumed):

| Parameter | Units |
|---|---|
| ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN | Wh/m^2 |
| PRECTOTCORR | mm/day |
| PS | kPa |
| RH2M | % |
| T2M | C |
| T2MDEW | C |
| WD10M | Degrees |
| WS10M | m/s |

Two of these differ from what is commonly assumed: `PRECTOTCORR` is
reported in mm/day and `ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN` in Wh/m^2. Values are used as
returned and never rescaled on an assumption.

**Time standard.** POWER hourly defaults to Local Solar Time, not UTC.
This pull explicitly requested `time-standard=UTC`
and the response header was verified to match.

![distribution](../results/figures/fig03_pm25_distribution.png)

| Statistic | Value (µg/m³) |
|---|---|
| n | 65,214 |
| mean | 93.68 |
| std | 83.04 |
| min | 0.2 |
| p01 | 7.0 |
| p05 | 15.0 |
| p25 | 35.0 |
| p50 | 66.0 |
| p75 | 130.0 |
| p90 | 206.0 |
| p95 | 252.0 |
| p99 | 360.0 |
| max | 985.0 |
| skew | 2.324 |
| excess kurtosis | 11.963 |

Exceedance of the Bangladesh national standards (Air Pollution (Control)
Rules 2022):

| Threshold | Hours above |
|---|---|
| 65 µg/m³ | 50.4% |
| 35 µg/m³ | 74.71% |

The distribution is strongly right-skewed, which is why the target is
modelled on a `log1p` scale while all metrics are reported in µg/m³, and
why sMAPE replaces MAPE.
